title: Heat-pump and refrigeration-chain evidence
principle: Installed stock, annual sales, thermal capacity, factory capacity and recorded equipment trade are different measures.

chain.detail: Copper, aluminium, steels, polymers, refrigerant feedstocks and sometimes permanent magnets.
Compressor, heat exchangers, expansion device, valves, fan or pumps, motor and controls.
Components are integrated into units matched to local voltage, climate, standards and building practices.
Sizing, emitters or ducts, electrical connection, pipework, commissioning and refrigerant handling.
Efficiency depends on temperatures, controls, building demand, maintenance and electricity prices.
Refrigerant is contained or reclaimed and metals/components enter repair, reuse or recycling routes.

global_2024.boundary: Heating-needs shares are service estimates. Manufacturing is nameplate thermal-output capacity, not unit sales or realised production.

global_recent.finding: Global building heat-pump sales peaked in 2022, slowed in 2023-24 and were broadly stable in 2025; technician shortages remained a bottleneck.
global_recent.boundary: The IEA global series combines technologies and region-specific definitions; it should not be spliced to the EU-21 unit series.

europe_history.scope: EU-21 as defined by EHPA's 2023 report
europe_history.boundary: EHPA market accounting includes eligible heating heat-pump categories and an assumed roughly 20-year life for stock. It is not the complete global market or a thermal-capacity series.

snapshot_rule: The 2024 and 2025 snapshots use different country sets and must not be treated as a like-for-like growth series.

technologies.name: Air-to-air
technologies.system: Often reversible heating and cooling; usually ducted or room units
technologies.exposure: Compressor, copper/aluminium coils, fans, electronics and refrigerant

technologies.name: Air-to-water
technologies.system: Feeds radiators, underfloor heating or hot-water storage
technologies.exposure: Unit plus hydronic balance of plant; retrofit temperatures and emitter sizing matter

technologies.name: Ground/water source
technologies.system: More stable source temperature but additional civil works
technologies.exposure: Pipe or borehole field can dominate project complexity and local content

technologies.name: Heat-pump water heater
technologies.source_sink: Ambient or exhaust heat → stored water
technologies.system: Dedicated hot-water appliance; CO2 systems are prominent in Japan
technologies.exposure: Tank, compressor, heat exchanger, refrigerant and controls

technologies.name: Industrial/district
technologies.system: Large, engineered installations with long planning cycles
technologies.exposure: Temperature lift, integration and project engineering outweigh simple unit counts

component_map.materials: Steels, copper windings, electronics; magnet use depends on motor design
Copper or aluminium tubes/fins, sometimes steel; joining and corrosion performance matter

component_map.role: Control pressure and swap heating/cooling direction
component_map.materials: Precision valves, sensors, controls and mixed alloys
Fluid choice changes pressures, safety class, servicing and factory design

component_map.role: Connects the machine to building and grid
component_map.materials: Pipework, ducts or emitters, cables, switchgear, pumps, storage and insulation

manufacturing.finding: More than 70% of building heat pumps sold in each major market were sourced domestically, but rotary-compressor production was mostly in China.
manufacturing.boundary: Final-unit localisation can coexist with upstream component concentration. Country-of-final-assembly is not component origin.

refrigerant_timeline.meaning: The ozone-depleting refrigerant transition becomes an international policy process.
The Montreal framework extends to an HFC phase-down because of climate impacts.
IEA reports new US-manufactured heat pumps had to use A2L refrigerants; product redesign affected market timing and supply.

refrigerant_rule: Refrigerant is not an interchangeable commodity: global-warming potential, flammability, pressure, efficiency, charge, standards and technician competence shape the usable choice.

series.boundary: All mine production; not heat-pump tubing or refined copper availability.
Primary metal production for all uses; not heat-exchanger manufacturing.
All rare earths; only some motor designs use permanent magnets.
All fluorspar uses; an upstream fluorine context, not refrigerant output.

material_histories.boundary: Economy-wide production context. These series do not measure heat-pump demand, component-grade supply, refrigerant production or recycled metal.

trade_context.boundary: HS 841861 excludes reversible air conditioners classified in heading 8415. Compressors and heat exchangers are mixed-use. Customs value is not installations, stock or thermal capacity.

boundaries: A reversible air conditioner used as primary heating can be a heat pump, but regional statistics do not count these consistently.
Unit sales cannot be added across categories without checking scope, capacity and country coverage.
Factory GW/year, shipped units, installed stock and useful heat have different denominators.
Heat-pump performance is a system outcome involving source temperature, delivery temperature, sizing, controls and the building envelope.
Bulk copper, aluminium, rare-earth and fluorspar histories do not identify component or refrigerant bottlenecks.
